name: AutomationCard
summary: A rule that runs on its own: when this, then that — and a switch.

a11y.apg: switch — turning the rule on and off is the Switch, a native checkbox with role=switch, so the keyboard is the platform's. The rest is a labelled article holding a DataList.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 29/08/2026 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). This ficha comes from the lineage that did not have check 30, so it declared keys with no measurement behind them — the merge of the two lineages on 29/08/2026 is what surfaced it. Confirmed: Space, which toggles the card's switch. The card itself is an article; the only interactive element it owns is that switch, and Space is the switch's key.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The WHEN. Rendered as the term/value pair the house already uses, not as prose: whoever reads this needs to find the condition without scanning a paragraph.

props.name: action
props.description: The THEN. A rule is a condition and a consequence — that pair is what separates this card from AgentCard, which is identity, and from TaskQueue, which is queued work.

props.name: enabled
props.description: Whether the rule is live. A disabled rule does not disappear and does not change colour: it recedes. Hiding it would hide the very rule someone is looking for in order to switch it back on.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Without it there is no switch — a read-only card stays read-only instead of showing a control that does nothing.

props.name: lastResult
props.description: How it went, as a Status — so the outcome is a word and not only a colour.

props.name: details
props.description: Extra rows appended after WHEN and THEN in the same list.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons for the footer. They enter as nodes, so whoever builds the button knows what it does — the reference dispatches by string, which trades the compiler for a verbal agreement.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the name, saying what the automation does. It is separate from name so the card can lay the two out on its own grid.

notes: The execution history did NOT come in. In the reference it is a tab with a table inside the same component; here DataGrid and EventStream already exist for that, and absorbing it would make the card answer for two contracts — the mistake TaskQueue refused in H.b.
